title: Aloe Socotrina
text: This remedy is characterized by a general feeling of heaviness and congestion, especially in the portal system and the rectum. It is useful in cases of haemorrhoids and chronic diarrhoea. There is a general lack of control over the anal sphincter. The patient is often a large, phlegmatic person. There is a marked tendency to portal congestion. Confused. Forgetful. Aversion to mental and physical labor. Headache, with a sensation of weight in the forehead. Vertigo. Eyes red and burning. Sensation of heat. Metallic taste. Tongue yellow and coated. Appetite poor. Thirst. Heaviness and pressure after eating. Distended and tender. Rumbling. Flatulence. Sharp pains in the region of the liver. Haemorrhoids, like bunches of grapes; purple, painful, and itching. Anus feels as if it were open. Constant desire for stool. Stool passes involuntarily while urinating or passing gas. Diarrhoea of thin, watery stools, with much gas. Frequent desire to urinate. Scanty urine. Aching and lameness in the limbs. Heaviness in the legs. Worse in the morning and in hot weather. Better from cold applications and in the open air. Compare: Aesculus; Collinsonia; Nux vom.; Sulphur. Second to sixth potency.
